mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for three consecutive weeks (-14.7 to -17.7). This autocorrelated downward momentum reflects persistent reduced shopping and leisure activity and is expected to continue without a new shock, pulling the next-28-day mean below the last-28-day mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell every week from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days rises above the last-28-day mean despite three prior weeks of decline, the momentum mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has reached its lowest point in the snapshot (-24.0) after a prior plateau near -22. A breach below -24 signals renewed or tightened restrictions on public transport use, which mechanically limits access to retail and recreation destinations, suppressing RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -24 points from baseline in a given week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped from -22.0 at t-1w to -24.0 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not decline further in the two weeks following a sub-(-24) TRANSIT reading, the threshold mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility is rising (2.9 to 5.1) at the same time WORKPLACES is recovering (-23.3 to -18.4). The joint rise indicates households are spending more time at home even as commuting resumes, implying errands are consolidated and discretionary retail trips are deprioritized, which combine to depress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises while WORKPLACES simultaneously rises for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL increased each week from 2.9 to 5.1 while WORKPLACES increased from -23.3 to -18.4
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite concurrent increases in both RESIDENTIAL and WORKPLACES, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has fallen sharply from 35.0 to 12.9 over four weeks, consistent with a seasonal transition away from outdoor recreation (e.g., cooling weather). As outdoor substitutes become less attractive, demand is expected to shift toward indoor retail and recreation venues, raising RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS declined from 35.0 at t-3w to 12.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 28 days despite the sustained seasonal drop in PARKS, the substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has risen for three consecutive weeks (-23.3 to -18.4). A continued week-over-week acceleration beyond 2 points signals strengthening commuting routines, which in the short run boosts incidental lunch-break and after-work retail visits, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES rises by more than 2 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -20.0 at t-1w to -18.4 at t-0w, a 1.6 point gain following larger prior gains
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise in the week immediately following a greater-than-2-point WORKPLACES increase, the short-horizon trigger is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility rebounded from -9.6 to -6.0 then stabilized near -7, indicating essential-goods shopping has normalized rather than spiking defensively. This signals the absence of acute precautionary stockpiling behavior, removing a prior drag and allowing RETAIL_REC to stabilize or modestly recover over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays within a 2-point band for two consecutive weeks after an initial rebound
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from -9.6 to -6.0 then held between -6.0 and -7.4
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 28 days despite GROCERY_PHARM stabilization, the normalization mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Under a reopening regime, the sustained narrowing of the WORKPLACES deficit (-23.3 to -18.4) reflects loosening policy restrictions on economic activity. This policy relaxation is expected to progressively extend to retail and recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks specifically while the reopening regime persists.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved by nearly 5 points over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC fails to rise over the next 28 days while WORKPLACES continues to improve, the policy-driven reopening mechanism is rejected; also rejected if the regime shifts to tightening.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of a steep PARKS decline (35.0 to 12.9) and a rising RESIDENTIAL trend (2.9 to 5.1) suggests a joint seasonal-behavioral shift toward indoor, home-centered life rather than toward retail substitution. When both signals move together in the same direction, they are expected to suppress rather than boost RETAIL_REC within one week, since reduced outdoor activity combines with increased home-dwelling rather than translating into store visits.
candidate_trigger: PARKS declines more than 10 points while RESIDENTIAL rises in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell nearly 9 points between t-2w and t-1w while RESIDENTIAL rose from 3.7 to 4.4
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a joint PARKS decline and RESIDENTIAL increase, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.
